mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the permission-matrix fact lets Alloy freely assign any (Role, OperationKind) pair to Allowed, immediately breaking LeastPrivilege (which requires specific denied cells) and PermissionCompleteness (which requires exactly 11 allowed cells).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PermissionMatrixViolation { Customer -> PostClaim in PermMatrix.Allowed and ComplianceReviewer -> PostDecision in PermMatrix.Allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the constraint that stops a single customer owning two in-flight applications. Injecting two in-flight applications for the same customer forces the FR-008 assertion to find a counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OneInFlightViolation { some disj a1, a2: LoanApplication | a1.appCustomer = a2.appCustomer and a1.appStatus = Submitted and a2.appStatus = UnderReview }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact allows a Decision's decidedBy field to reference a User other than the application's assignedOfficer. The injection forces a decided application whose decider differs from the assigned officer, violating FR-013.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DecisionByWrongOfficer { some a: LoanApplication | some a.appDecision and (some a.assignedOfficer) and a.appDecision.decidedBy != a.assignedOfficer }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the requirement for an initial audit event allows a LoanApplication to exist with zero ApplicationEvent entries. The injection creates an application with no events at all, directly violating AuditCompleteness.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MissingInitialEvent { some a: LoanApplication | no e: ApplicationEvent | e.evtApp = a }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the uniqueness constraint on (application, prevStatus, newStatus) triples allows two event atoms to represent duplicate transitions — exactly what append-only forbids. The injection forces two events with the same application and same (prevStatus, newStatus) pair.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DuplicateAuditEntry { some disj e1, e2: ApplicationEvent | e1.evtApp = e2.evtApp and e1.prevStatus = e2.prevStatus and e1.newStatus = e2.newStatus }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the status/officer coupling constraint allows a Submitted application to have an assignedOfficer, or an UnderReview application to have none. The injection creates a Submitted application with an assigned officer, violating the biconditional enforced by the data-model CHECK.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_SubmittedWithOfficer { some a: LoanApplication | a.appStatus = Submitted and some a.assignedOfficer }
